footer.builtWith: Built with Fougere — this site runs on the framework it documents.

home.title: TypeScript business code first. Deployment and API later.
home.subtitle: Declare your domain once. Validation, tables, API and forms derive from it, and one config line decides where each part runs.
home.plateCredit: R. Siélain, Atlas de poche des plantes des champs, pl. 124, 1895
home.codeText: The green marble is your business code: plain classes that do the work and ask for what they need. No route, no setup, no server required.
home.schemaText: The white marble is your schema: you describe a post once, and your code uses it everywhere.
home.derivationText: The globe is what comes out of that one class, on both sides. Nothing to keep in sync.
home.derivationCalls: what calls you — REST, GraphQL, forms, client types
home.derivationCalled: what you call — tables, migrations, ports
home.derivationCaption: One field added to an entity: the table, the form and the API follow.
home.gradientText: Where each part runs, and what answers each port: one line each, the same code. It does not even have to be written in TypeScript.
home.gradientCaption: One line in fougere.config.ts: the blog answers from its own process, and the page keeps working.
home.sameText: One process or two, it is the same code. Everything around it was derived or chosen.
home.tryText: TypeScript business code first. Deployment and API later.
home.auditTitle: Don't take our word for it.
home.auditText: Paste this prompt into the agent that already knows your codebase. It counts where your commits go and what each kind of change costs, and it reports what adopting Fougere would cost just as carefully.
